newsitem.title: NORWAY: Salomon Brothers favour Norway's biggest banks.
newsitem.headline: Salomon Brothers favour Norway's biggest banks.

text.p: Norway's top commercial banks, Den norske Bank (DnB) and Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse, remain attractive on price/book and relative yield valuations, Salomon Brothers said in a market update on Monday.
DnB will present the 1996 result on February 12, followed by Christiania on February 19.
"The Norwegian banks are returning to normal earnings in 1997-1998 as their tax shields run down and provisioning charges turn positive again," Salomon Brothers said.
"Both Christiania Bank and DnB nonetheless remain attractive on price/book and relative yield valuations."
Christiania Bank's 1996 earnings will be depressed by the fourth-quarter 228 million crown restructuring charge announced on December 31, the report noted.
"The cost savings resulting from the restructuring and staff reductions (nine percent minimal headcount reduction over 24 months) should begin to flow through meaningfully in 1998," it said.
DnB announced its cost-cutting programme earlier in 1996.
"Another variable in the equation has been the availability of Christiania Bank's remaining tax-loss carryforwards, contingent as they are on appellate court decisions," it said.
"We are taking the conservative approach recommended by the bank and assuming that the contested 2.7 billion crowns is not available for use in 1997-1998," Salmon Brothers said.
If Christiania eventually wins it judicial review, the bank will be rewarded the full amount with interest. For comparison, DnB's tax protection is largely depleted.
Seven analysts polled by Reuters forecast recently that Christiania Bank would post pre-tax operating profits of 1.86 billion crowns, down from 2.79 billion in 1995.
DnB is expected to book pre-tax operating profits of 2.82 billion crowns, up from 2.63 billion crowns in 1995, according to seven analysts polled by Reuters.
